sources.title: Libya Country Brief
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Global Information and Early Warning System
sources.temporal_coverage: Weather and crop conditions through July 2026; 2026 harvest and 2026/27 import forecasts.
sources.methodology: FAO GIEWS synthesis of rainfall, crop, price and food-security data.
sources.limitations: Forecasts are not verified outcomes; no climate attribution or detailed local food-security estimates.

sources.title: Rapid flood impact assessment on water management infrastructure and agriculture in Eastern Libya in 2023
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment of the September 2023 floods; FAO summary published May 2025.
sources.methodology: FAO summary of a rapid geospatial assessment using flood extent, land cover, irrigated cropland, population and farmer-vulnerability indicators.
sources.limitations: The linked full report download returned 403; only the complete official FAO summary page was inspected, so detailed underlying methods and district tables were not reviewed.

sources.title: Situational Assessment of The South of Libya 2024
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator's Office in Libya
sources.temporal_coverage: 2024 situational assessment, published 19 January 2025; recommendations are not evidence of later delivery.
sources.methodology: UN inter-agency assessment of governance, services, social cohesion and environmental conditions in southern Libya.
sources.limitations: The PDF exceeded reader limits; claims use only official indexed executive-summary and climate/DRR excerpts.

sources.title: The United Nations Libya Annual Results Report 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Reported United Nations results achieved during 2025; report published 3 May 2026.
sources.methodology: United Nations country-team annual results report describing partner-supported outputs and reported beneficiaries.
sources.limitations: The 46.9 MB report exceeded the reader limit; claims use only official indexed excerpts on printed p.34 and are implementer-reported, not an independent impact evaluation.

claims.locator: FAO GIEWS brief, reference date 16 July 2026, rainfall and crop conditions
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports dry October-November 2025 weather delayed planting and reduced area; March 2026 rainfall improved some regions but remained well below average in cereal-producing Al Jabal al Akhdar.
claims.limitations: Weather observations are not climate attribution.

claims.locator: FAO GIEWS brief, 2026 cereal production and import forecast
claims.paraphrase: FAO forecasts 2026 cereal output near 150,000 tonnes, almost 20 percent below the five-year average, and 2026/27 cereal imports of 3.3 million tonnes.
claims.limitations: Forecasts are not final figures; Libya relies heavily on imports.

claims.locator: FAO GIEWS brief, May 2026 food-price and assistance conditions
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports 18 percent annual food inflation in May 2026; political and economic instability undermines livelihoods and services, while funding limits assistance to refugees, migrants and internally displaced people.
claims.limitations: National summary; no weather-to-price or weather-to-assistance causal finding.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FAO links instability to weaker livelihoods and services.

claims.locator: Official FAO summary, assessment results for Benghazi
claims.paraphrase: FAO's rapid assessment reports that extreme rainfall and dam collapses caused catastrophic September 2023 flooding in eastern Libya; Benghazi was the most affected area, with 36,245 hectares flooded.
claims.limitations: The accessible summary provides the Benghazi aggregate but not locality-level exposure tables or the full assessment methods.

claims.paraphrase: The UN names Sebha, Murzuq, Ghat, Kufra and Ubari among municipalities facing heat, water scarcity and drought, alongside service deficits, conflict and weak governance; women, youth and displaced people face disproportionate service gaps.
claims.limitations: No isolated climate-to-conflict causal effect is established.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The summary calls southern vulnerabilities compounded by conflict and governance deficits, and challenges interconnected.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed p.1; Environmental Protection, Climate Change Adaptation and Disaster Risk Reduction, printed p.29
claims.paraphrase: The assessment says unresolved conflicts in Murzuq and Kufra eroded cohesion and stalled reconciliation; climate adaptation and disaster-risk efforts are fragmented and underfunded, leaving communities vulnerable.
claims.limitations: It does not attribute adaptation shortfalls to conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It links instability and unresolved conflict to eroded cohesion and stalled reconciliation.

claims.locator: Printed p.34, Hayat water panels and renewable-water installations
claims.paraphrase: The UN report says Hayat water panels supplied sustainable water access and livelihood support to more than 150,000 people in southern Libya in 2025; four desalination units and ten solar systems served Ubari, Ghat, Tahala and Alberkit.
claims.limitations: Reported 2025 reach and installations are implementer-reported outputs; the report excerpt provides no independent outcome evaluation.

claims.locator: Printed p.34, Qatroun wells and Yefren integrated water-resource management
claims.paraphrase: The report states restored wells provided water access to 75 percent of Qatroun's population, while a Yefren integrated water-resource plan delivered long-distance water to 49,000 residents, 52 percent of them women.
claims.limitations: These are reported outputs for 2025; the excerpt does not describe service continuity or independent verification.

search_audit.query: Libya regional crop and rainfall anomalies, eastern flood impacts and named local agricultural vulnerability official FAO evidence
search_audit.outcome: FAO GIEWS provides a current Al Jabal al Akhdar rainfall and cereal outlook; FAO's eastern flood assessment summary reports Benghazi inundation and an assessment of irrigated land and farmer vulnerability.

search_audit.query: Southern Libya climate water scarcity drought, conflict, governance, displacement and social cohesion primary UN sources
search_audit.outcome: The UN South assessment explicitly describes climatic and environmental vulnerabilities as compounded by conflict, governance deficits and underdevelopment, while identifying specific social-cohesion effects in Murzuq and Kufra; it does not isolate climate-caused violence.

search_audit.query: Libya conflict and fragility effects on climate adaptation, disaster risk management, water and infrastructure official evidence
search_audit.outcome: The South assessment reports fragmented and underfunded adaptation/DRR and separately identifies conflict-related erosion of social cohesion; it does not state that conflict caused those programmatic deficits. FAO documents catastrophic flood and dam-collapse exposure in eastern Libya.

search_audit.query: Libya subnational climate-resilient water supply, solar desalination, wells and water-resource management results official report
search_audit.outcome: The UN 2025 Annual Results Report's indexed p.34 passage reports localized water access outputs in southern municipalities; these are agency-reported results, not independently evaluated impacts.

gaps: The FAO July 2026 cereal harvest and import values are forecasts, not verified final outcomes, and are not attributed to anthropogenic climate change.

The full FAO eastern Libya assessment and the full UN South assessment and UN Annual Results Report exceeded reader limits or returned an access error; claims are confined to the accessible official summary or indexed excerpts.

Sources describe connected climate, governance and conflict vulnerabilities in southern Libya but do not establish a causal climate-to-violence pathway or show that conflict obstructed a specific adaptation project.
UN annual results describe 2025 water-service outputs; service continuity, distributional reach and independent outcome impacts were not assessed in the accessible passage.
